intro: Zierenberg is a small town in the hills north-west of Kassel, in northern Hesse. On an open meadow a couple of kilometres east of it stands a broad beech that a reader photographed in November, its crown still holding some copper leaves. They put its girth at about five metres and its age at roughly 183 years. We have not yet seen a measurement or a record of it, and we would like to.

trees.story:
A reader sent us this beech from the hills near Zierenberg, north-west of Kassel in northern Hesse, photographed in November with the last of its copper leaves still on the twigs.

It stands on its own on a sloping meadow. Beeches in a forest race upwards on long bare trunks; with open grass all round it, this one has spread instead. A short, heavy trunk opens low into dozens of limbs that fan up and out into a crown almost as wide as it is tall, a dome of fine grey twigs against the clouds. Its fallen leaves lie in a rust-brown drift on the grass below and spill down the slope, and a hedge of scrub and smaller trees runs along the bank behind it.

The reader puts its girth at about five metres and its age at roughly 183 years. Those figures are theirs: we have not seen a measurement or a record of when it was planted. If you know this tree, a name the village gives it, or who keeps the meadow, tell us here and we will add it.

Go in late autumn, as the reader did, when the crown turns copper, and walk round to the downhill side to see how low the limbs leave the trunk.
